title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: sanctitas not second life; Adam vs Christ; Sed haec obiter
pass_a_gloss: And so just as in the body there was not a double life, of which one would be placed in health, so I do not think the sanctity of the soul increases the number of lives with which Adam was endowed. For I observe a great difference between Adam's sanctity and ours in Christ. That was natural, created together with human nature, and, unless it had been lost, to be propagated according to the laws of nature, and therefore mutable: but this depends on the supernatural gift of the Holy Spirit fallen from Christ the head into us his members, by which we are regenerated, vivified, and as it were animated and ruled. Adam's sanctity was a condition of that life of Adam which you call animal, without which he could not have been created by the most just and most holy God, and by which it came about that Adam was well fitted to natural objects. Ours depends wholly on supernatural revelation, tends wholly to a supernatural object, and carries us far above that natural and animal and mutable condition of Adam. And so it is called divine nature by Peter, and the image of the glory of Christ by Paul. But these things by the way: for they do nothing for the matter we are treating.
pass_b_english: Just as the body did not have a double life with one part seated in health, so I do not think the soul's sanctity adds to the tally of lives Adam had. I see a great gap between Adam's sanctity and ours in Christ. His was natural, created with human nature, and—had it not been lost—would have been passed on by nature's laws, and so was changeable. Ours hangs on the supernatural gift of the Holy Spirit come down from Christ the head into us his members, by which we are regenerated, made alive, and as it were animated and ruled.

Adam's sanctity was a condition of that animal life of his, as you call it—without which the most just and holy God could not have made him, and by which he was well fitted to natural objects. Ours hangs wholly on supernatural revelation, aims wholly at a supernatural object, and lifts us far above Adam's natural, animal, changeable state. So Peter calls it divine nature, and Paul the image of Christ's glory. But this is by the way; it does not touch the point in hand.
source_text: Itaque quemadmodum in corpore non erat duplex vita, quarum altera posita esset in sanitate, sic non arbitror sanctitatem animae augere numerum vitarum, quibus praeditus fuit Adamus. Magnum enim discrimen observo inter Adami & nostram in Christo sanctitatem. Illa naturalis fuit simul cum natura humana & creata, &, nisi amissa fuisset, propaganda secundum leges naturae, ac propterea mutabilis: haec vero pendet ex dono supernaturali Spiritus Sancti a Christo capite in nos eius membra delapso, quo regeneramur, vivificamur, & veluti animamur ac regimur. Sanctitas Adami conditio erat eius vitae Adami, quam animalem appellas, sine qua creari non potuit a Deo justissimo sanctissimoque, & qua fiebat ut Adamus esset bene comparatus ad objecta naturalia. Nostra tota pendet a revelatione supernaturali, tota tendit in objectum supernaturale, nosque supra conditionem illam naturalem & animalem & mutabilem Adami longe evehit. Itaque natura divina a Petro appellatur, & imago gloriae Christi a Paulo. Sed haec obiter: nihil enim faciunt ad rem quam agimus.
